title: Sandbox pre-flight is a silent no-op for migrated repos
description:
FAIL-OPEN in Phase 1s own deliverable. cloud/sandbox/preflight.sh still parses the pre-48d markdown ## Environment section of .tick/config.md. That section no longer exists in a migrated repo — the checks now live in [environment.commands] in runners.toml — so the run-start gate finds nothing to run and SILENTLY PASSES for every migrated repo.

This is precisely the parity point 3q2 predicted when it noted preflight.sh mirrors the runners single-inline-code-span rule; it was recorded on 48d and the migration did not carry it across. A pre-flight that always passes is worse than no pre-flight: it reports a green environment check on a broken environment, which is the failure mode this whole epic keeps catching in other guises.

Fix, same shape as 79x used: have the entrypoint ask tk for the environment checks rather than parsing config files in bash. That removes the second parser permanently instead of teaching it a second format. Include a test that a migrated repo actually RUNS its checks and that a failing check still stops the boot nonzero with the failing check named.

acceptance_criteria: A migrated repo running the sandbox entrypoint executes its [environment.commands] checks; a failing check exits nonzero naming the check; a repo with no environment checks is distinguishable in the log from a repo whose checks were not found; no markdown parsing remains in preflight.sh.
